$comment: Demo accounts, migrated from legacy db/db_data/demo_users.json.
Role mapping from the legacy vocabulary — each is a decision, not a rename:
legacy SUPER_ADMIN -> SYSTEM_ADMIN   platform-wide, schoolId MUST be null
legacy ADMIN       -> SCHOOL_ADMIN   scoped to one school
legacy SUPERVISOR  -> (dropped)      the new system has no supervisor role;
inventing one to preserve a legacy
label would add an unenforced
permission surface.
SYSTEM_ADMIN and SCHOOL_ADMIN are NOT the same account and must never be
merged. PLATFORM_WIDE_ROLES puts SYSTEM_ADMIN outside any school, so it
sees every school; SCHOOL_ADMIN is bound to sch_demo and sees only that.
Seeding one account with both roles would make it impossible to test that
the boundary actually holds.
`password` is present because these are development accounts and a seeded
credential nobody can read is useless. The seed prints them.
The 'User' section is named after the Prisma model, and nested objects are
named after the models they create: learnerProfile -> LearnerProfile,
guardianProfile -> GuardianProfile. Fields ending in 'Key' are references
the seed resolves to ids (schoolKey -> School.id, gradeKey -> Grade.id).
Every user carries phone, status and locale explicitly rather than relying
on column defaults. A default is a decision the file cannot show you: with
status written out, suspending a demo account to exercise the blocked
sign-in path is a one-word edit here instead of a hand-run UPDATE.
All nine accounts appear in the development sign-in box. arch:check fails
if this file and web/src/features/auth/demo-credentials.dev.ts disagree,
because a stale button returns a 401 that looks like a broken login.

User.$comment: A second author, because SUBMIT and APPROVE must be two different people for the separation to mean anything.
A different grade, so roster scoping is testable rather than assumed.
